mainEntity.name: How much does a Volvo XC90 T6 engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A B4204T27 or B6304T4 replacement typically costs £1,800-£5,500 supply-only, depending on condition (used, reconditioned, or rebuilt). Full supply & fit through a specialist adds approximately £600-£1,200 in labour. Used B4204T27: £1,200-£2,200. Reconditioned B4204T27: £2,200-£3,800. Rebuilt B4204T27: £3,000-£5,000. Fitting labour: 10-16 hours at £65/hr indie rates.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the T5 and T6 petrol engines in the XC90?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both are 2.0-litre four-cylinder Drive-E engines, but the T5 is single-turbocharged (254hp) while the T6 adds a supercharger for low-end response (320hp). The T6's twin-charged setup - turbocharger and supercharger - delivers instant low-end torque and strong top-end power. T5 (B4204T23): 254hp, single turbo, simpler design. T6 (B4204T27): 320hp, twin-charged (turbo + supercharger), more complex. The T5 avoids supercharger-related failure modes.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Volvo XC90 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: This depends entirely on your XC90's value and condition. As a rule of thumb: vehicle worth under £4,000 - a used engine or repair typically makes more sense; vehicle worth £4,000-£10,000 - reconditioned is viable if keeping the car 2+ years; vehicle worth £10,000+ - rebuilt engine with warranty is usually the best long-term value. For a well-maintained XC90 with a sound body and transmission, engine replacement is almost always cheaper than buying a comparable replacement vehicle.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Volvo XC90 petrol engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical XC90 petrol engine swap takes 2-5 working days, depending on the workshop's workload and whether supply-only or supply & fit is chosen. Supply-only: 1-3 days for delivery. Supply & fit: 3-5 days total (including delivery and fitting). Mobile fitting: may take longer as the fitter travels to your location.

mainEntity.name: Which XC90 petrol engine is the most reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The naturally aspirated 3.2-litre SI6 (B6324S5) is widely considered the most reliable XC90 petrol engine - it has no turbo, no supercharger, and a simple, robust design. The five-cylinder 2.5T (B5254T12) is also well-regarded, though the timing belt requires regular replacement. Among the Drive-E engines, the T5 (single-turbo) is simpler and therefore less prone to failure than the twin-charged T6.

mainEntity.name: Does a replacement XC90 petrol engine come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - every rebuilt and reconditioned engine supplied through EnginesMarket carries a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Used engines typically come with a shorter warranty (30-90 days), so always check the terms before purchasing. Rebuilt engines: 12+ months unlimited mileage. Reconditioned engines: 12+ months unlimited mileage. Used engines: 30-90 days (varies by supplier).

historyTimeline.h2: Volvo XC90 T5 / T6 Petrol - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Volvo XC90 petrol range launched in 2002 with the 2.5-litre five-cylinder turbo (T5) and the 2.9-litre six-cylinder twin-turbo (T6). The first-generation petrol lineup expanded to include a 3.2-litre naturally aspirated six-cylinder and a 4.4-litre V8, before the second-generation 2015 XC90 introduced the all-new Drive-E 2.0-litre four-cylinder family - with the T5 single-turbo and T6 twin-charged (turbocharged and supercharged) units.

milestones.description: 2.5T B5254T2, 2.5-litre five-cylinder turbo, 210hp - first-generation XC90 launch petrol
T6 B6294T, 2.9-litre six-cylinder twin-turbo, 272hp - range-topping petrol joins the line-up
3.2 B6324S, 3.2-litre naturally aspirated six-cylinder, 238hp - replaced the 2.5T
V8 B8444S, 4.4-litre V8 naturally aspirated, 315hp - Yamaha-designed V8, limited production
T6 B6304T4, 3.0-litre six-cylinder turbo, 304hp - replaced the 2.9T, Ward's 10 Best Engines 2011
Second-generation XC90 (SPA) launches - T5 B4204T23, 2.0-litre four-cylinder turbo, 254hp
T5 B4204T20, 2.0-litre four-cylinder turbo, 249hp - lower-output T5 variant
Petrol T5 and T6 phased out in favour of B5 and B6 mild-hybrid petrol units

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every petrol engine fitted to the Volvo XC90 - from the early five-cylinder T5 to the twin-charged Drive-E T6 - is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Volvo XC90 T5 / T6 Petrol Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The XC90 petrol range is broadly reliable, particularly the naturally aspirated 3.2-litre SI6 and the five-cylinder 2.5T. However, two major failure patterns dominate replacement demand: **timing belt failure on first-generation petrol engines** and **supercharger/turbocharger issues on the second-generation twin-charged T6**. Rebuilt engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Belt Failure - Why the First-Generation Volvo XC90 Petrol Engines Fail Catastrophically
problems.rootCause: First-generation XC90 petrol engines use timing belts, not chains. The belt can stretch, jump teeth, or snap entirely - when this happens, pistons strike valves, destroying the engine. The manufacturer's recommended replacement interval is critical, and some owners report failure before the official interval.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full timing belt kit (belt, tensioner, idler, water pump recommended)
repairOptions.longevity: The only sensible approach - replace proactively at or before 96,000-108,000 miles / 10 years

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, full engine rebuild or replacement
repairOptions.longevity: Only if belt has already snapped - catastrophic damage means replacement is the only option

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical first-generation XC90 petrol (2002-2014) is worth approximately £2,000-£10,000 `[THIRD-PARTY]`. For vehicles under £3,000, evaluate whether a preventative belt replacement (£400-£800 specialist) makes sense relative to the car's overall condition. For vehicles worth £3,000+, preventative replacement is excellent value for money.
problems.recommendation: This is simple - **replace the timing belt proactively**. The cost of preventative replacement (£400-£800 at an independent specialist) is a fraction of the £2,500-£5,500 cost of a replacement engine after belt failure. Check your service history: if the belt hasn't been done and you're approaching 100,000 miles or 10 years, book it in immediately.

problems.h4: Supercharger Failure - Why the Volvo XC90 T6 Twin-Charged Engine Loses Low-End Power
problems.rootCause: The T6's supercharger is engaged at low RPMs to provide immediate throttle response before the turbo spools up. The supercharger clutch is a known failure point - when it wears, you'll feel a delay or cutting in-and-out of boost at low RPMs. The supercharger intake seal can also fail, causing boost leaks and hesitation on acceleration. Some owners report a characteristic rattle or grinding noise from the supercharger area.

repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early - restores low-end power

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace the intake seal on the supercharger
Supply & fit, upgraded supercharger components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Only if supercharger failure has caused secondary damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical second-generation XC90 T6 (2015-2020) is worth approximately £12,000-£35,000 `[THIRD-PARTY]`. Supercharger repairs (£400-£900 specialist) are comfortably within vehicle value and represent a good investment. Full engine replacement is only justified if secondary damage has occurred.
problems.recommendation: For most B4204T27 owners with supercharger issues, clutch or seal replacement is the right call - it's cost-effective and restores full performance. Don't ignore the warning signs; delayed action can lead to more extensive damage. Note that the T5 (single-turbo, no supercharger) avoids this failure mode entirely.

problems.h4: PCV System Failure - Whistling Noise and Oil Leaks Across All XC90 Petrol Engines
problems.affectedModels: All Volvo XC90 petrol engines (B4204T23/T20, B4204T27, B6304T4, B5254T12, B6324S5)
problems.rootCause: The Positive Crankcase Ventilation (PCV) system regulates crankcase pressure. On Volvo SI6 engines (B6304T4, B6324S5), the PCV oil trap diaphragm is a common failure point - when it tears, it produces a whistling noise from the top of the engine at idle. On Drive-E engines, PCV blockages can cause oil leaks from seals and gaskets.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace the PCV oil trap diaphragm
repairOptions.longevity: Simple, inexpensive fix for the whistling noise

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Clean or replace the PCV system components
repairOptions.longevity: Resolves oil leaks and pressure issues

repairOptions.specialistPrice: N/A (PCV repair is not a reason for full replacement)
repairOptions.longevity: PCV issues alone do not justify full engine replacement

problems.vehicleValueCheck: PCV repairs (£150-£500 specialist) are inexpensive relative to any XC90's value. This is a maintenance item, not a replacement trigger.
problems.recommendation: Address PCV issues promptly - they're inexpensive to fix and, if ignored, can lead to oil leaks and, in extreme cases, oil starvation. The whistling noise from the top of the engine on SI6 models is the classic symptom; don't ignore it.
